title: 1993 AHSME Problem 24
statement: A box contains \(3\) shiny pennies and \(4\) dull pennies. One by one, pennies are drawn at random from the box and not replaced. If the probability is \(\frac{a}{b}\) that it will take more than four draws until the third shiny penny appears and \(\frac{a}{b}\) is in lowest terms, then \(a+b=\)

solutions.text: The shiny pennies occupy a uniformly chosen \(3\)-element subset of the \(7\) draw positions. There are \(\binom73=35\) possibilities. The third shiny penny appears by draw \(4\) exactly when all three shiny positions lie among the first four, which occurs in \(\binom43=4\) cases. The requested probability is \[ 1-\frac4{35}=\frac{31}{35}. \] Therefore \(a+b=31+35=66.\) Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: View the three shiny pennies as occupying three of seven draw positions
Subtract the cases in which all three shiny pennies occur among the first four positions
